rejected.title: International humanitarian law
card: International humanitarian law (IHL) is the set of rules that apply during armed conflict. It aims to limit suffering, not to decide whether going to war is lawful.
The four Geneva Conventions of 1949 are its core. They protect people who are not fighting or can no longer fight: civilians, prisoners of war and the wounded and sick.
Parties to a conflict must treat these people humanely. Prisoners of war must not be tortured, and civilians must not be deliberately attacked.
IHL binds all sides in an armed conflict. A breach of its rules can be a war crime, for which individuals can be held responsible.
rejected.remember: IHL governs how a war is fought and protects people who are not fighting.

a.q: Which question does international humanitarian law mainly answer?
opts: How must people be treated during an armed conflict?
Is it lawful for a state to go to war at all?
Which state should lead a peace operation?
How should a war be paid for after it ends?
a.why: IHL sets rules for conduct during armed conflict, such as humane treatment of civilians and prisoners. The question of whether a state may use force at all is a separate matter, so that option is tempting but wrong.
a.clue: IHL is about conduct during fighting.

b.q: During an armed conflict, one army captures enemy soldiers and holds them in a camp. Under the Geneva Conventions, what must it do?
opts: Treat them humanely and not torture them
Release them once the fighting in that area stops
Treat them as civilians who are not protected
Hold them without rules because they are enemies
b.why: Captured soldiers are prisoners of war, and the Geneva Conventions require humane treatment and ban torture. Being an enemy does not remove this protection, so holding them without rules is wrong.
b.clue: Prisoners of war are protected, even though they were fighting.

draft.title: International humanitarian law
card: International humanitarian law (IHL) is the set of rules for how armed conflict is fought. It aims to limit suffering.
The four Geneva Conventions of 1949 are its core. They protect people who are not fighting or can no longer fight: civilians, prisoners of war, and the wounded and sick.
These people must be treated humanely. Civilians must not be deliberately attacked, and prisoners of war must not be tortured. Wounded enemy fighters must be cared for.
IHL binds all sides, whoever started the war and whether or not the war was lawful. A side cannot ignore the rules because its enemy does. Serious breaches can be war crimes.
draft.remember: IHL protects people who are not fighting, and it binds every side in a conflict.

a.q: A state starts a war that many countries call unlawful. Do the Geneva rules still bind its army?
opts: Yes, the rules apply to every side in the conflict
No, only the side that acted lawfully must follow them
No, the rules apply only after the war has ended
Yes, but only for how it treats enemy soldiers
a.why: IHL governs how fighting is conducted, and it applies to all sides whether or not the war was lawful. The idea that only the lawful side is bound is tempting, but it would let the protections depend on who started the war.
a.clue: IHL does not depend on who started the war.

b.q: An army finds an enemy soldier, badly wounded and no longer fighting. Its commander learns the enemy has ignored the rules. What must the army do?
opts: Give him medical care, as he is no longer fighting
Refuse care, as the enemy has ignored the rules
Give care only if the enemy starts following the rules
Give care only if he agrees to share information
b.why: A wounded soldier who is no longer fighting is protected, and he must be cared for. The protection does not depend on the enemy's conduct, so waiting for the enemy to follow the rules is wrong, even though it can seem fair.
b.clue: A side cannot ignore the rules because its enemy does.

a.best: Yes, the rules apply to every side in the conflict

b.best: Give him medical care, as he is no longer fighting

check.summary: No problems found. The card correctly states that IHL binds all sides whatever the lawfulness of the war, and that protections do not depend on the enemy's conduct. Both questions have one clearly right answer that matches the writer's explanations.
